# FacetViz — chart and FacetTable generation guide for coding agents

FacetViz is a dependency-free TypeScript/SVG charting library with a declarative
configuration API plus a semantic HTML table component for charts inside cells.
Use this file to generate valid, readable, maintainable chart or table options.
Capability guide: `docs/features.html`. Full API: `docs/API.md`. Executable
examples: `docs/examples-data.js`.

## Agent output contract

When asked to create a chart or chart table:

1. Identify the analytical goal before choosing a type: comparison, trend,
   distribution, relationship, composition, range, hierarchy, flow, schedule,
   or small multiples.
2. Inspect the data shape, units, cardinality, missing values, and whether x is
   categorical, numeric, or time-based.
3. Produce one complete `ChartOptions` object with `series` present. For a
   semantic table with charts in cells, produce `FacetTableOptions<Row>` with
   `rows` and `columns` instead. Do not invent option names or chart types.
4. Prefer the simplest chart that answers the question. Add advanced options
   only when the data or request justifies them.
5. Include a descriptive title, axis titles with units, useful series names,
   tooltips, and an accessibility description unless the surrounding UI already
   supplies the same information.
6. State any material assumption, such as interpreting Unix values as
   milliseconds or treating categories as ordered.
7. For application code, create one chart instance and update it. Do not mount a
   new instance into the same container on every data/theme change.
8. When a `ChartOptions` configuration comes from generated JSON or another
   untrusted source, call `validateChartOptions(candidate)` and repair every
   error before render. Use `validation:{mode:'error'}` when later runtime
   updates must be guarded too. Do not pass a whole `FacetTableOptions` object
   to `validateChartOptions`; it validates chart options, not table structure.

```ts
import { FacetViz } from 'facetviz';

const chart = new FacetViz(container, options);
// container: HTMLElement or CSS selector string
// options.series is required
```

The default `facetviz` entrypoint includes every renderer. When bundle size is
important, use `facetviz/core` and import each required family before validation
or construction:

```ts
import { FacetViz, validateChartOptions } from 'facetviz/core';
import 'facetviz/series/line';   // line, spline, step
import 'facetviz/series/pie';    // pie, donut
```

Other family paths mirror renderer module names; `column` also registers bar
and butterfly, `range` registers both area-range aliases, and `scatter`
registers jitter. Use `facetviz/series/all` when dynamic configurations may use
arbitrary chart types. If validation reports `chart.type.unknown` with the core
entrypoint, import the matching family before changing the chart configuration.

## FacetTable: values and charts in table cells

Use `FacetTable` when each data record should remain a semantic HTML table row
and one or more columns should contain compact FacetViz charts. Use a normal
`FacetViz` chart for a standalone visualization and `trellis` for repeated SVG
panels that do not need native table cells.

```ts
import { FacetTable } from 'facetviz';

// `ChartTable` is an exported alias, but prefer the canonical `FacetTable` name.

interface ProductRow {
  product: string;
  revenue: number;
  growth: number;
  trend: number[];
}

const table = new FacetTable<ProductRow>('#performance', {
  caption: 'Product performance',
  rows: [
    { product: 'Atlas', revenue: 128400, growth: 0.124,
      trend: [64,69,72,70,78,82,86,91,96,104,112,128] },
    { product: 'Beacon', revenue: 86900, growth: 0.071,
      trend: [48,51,49,54,58,57,61,63,60,66,72,87] },
  ],
  columns: [
    { key: 'product', header: 'Product', sortable: true, filterable: true,
      horizontalAlign: 'left', verticalAlign: 'top' },
    { key: 'revenue', header: 'Revenue', sortable: true,
      horizontalAlign: 'right', verticalAlign: 'bottom',
      format: '{value:$,.0f}' },
    { key: 'growth', header: 'YoY', horizontalAlign: 'center',
      format: '{value:.1%}' },
    { key: 'trend', header: '12-month trend', width: 240,
      chart: {
        type: 'sparkline', height: 44, minWidth: 180, scale: 'shared',
        options: {
          plotOptions: { sparkline: { sparkline: { min: true, max: true } } },
          tooltip: { valueSuffix: 'k' },
        },
      } },
  ],
  pagination: { pageSize: 25, pageSizeOptions: [10,25,50,100] },
});
```

### FacetTable options

```ts
interface FacetTableOptions<Row extends object> {
  rows: Row[];                              // required
  columns: FacetTableColumnDefinition<Row>[]; // required, at least one leaf
  caption?: string;
  className?: string;
  layout?: FacetTableLayoutOptions;
  emptyText?: string;                       // default 'No data'
  appearance?: FacetTableAppearanceOptions;
  style?: FacetTableStyleOptions<Row>;
  pagination?: boolean | FacetTablePaginationOptions; // default false
}

interface FacetTableRowMetadata {
  rowType?: 'detail'|'subtotal'|'grandTotal';
  groupPath?: ReadonlyArray<unknown>;
}

interface FacetTableColumn<Row extends object> {
  key: keyof Row & string;                  // property read from every row
  header?: string;                          // defaults to key
  width?: number|string;                    // number means pixels
  horizontalAlign?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
  align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';          // compatibility alias
  verticalAlign?: 'top'|'middle'|'bottom';  // default middle
  role?: 'dimension'|'value';               // inferred when omitted
  style?: Record<string,string|number> |
          ((value, row: Row, rowIndex: number) => Record<string,string|number>);
  headerStyle?: Record<string,string|number>;
  sortable?: boolean | {
    initialDirection?: 'asc'|'desc';
    compare?: (a, b, rowA: Row, rowB: Row) => number;
  };
  filterable?: boolean | {
    initialValue?: string;
    placeholder?: string;
    predicate?: (value: unknown, filterValue: string, row: Row,
                 rowIndex: number) => boolean;
  };
  format?: string;                          // normal value cells only
  formatter?: (value, row: Row, rowIndex: number) => string|Node;
  chart?: FacetTableCellChartOptions<Row>;  // presence makes this a chart cell
}

type FacetTableColumnDefinition<Row extends object> =
  FacetTableColumn<Row> | FacetTableColumnGroup<Row>;

interface FacetTableColumnGroup<Row extends object> {
  header: string;
  columns: FacetTableColumnDefinition<Row>[]; // leaf columns or nested groups
  horizontalAlign?: 'left'|'center'|'right'; // default center
  align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';           // compatibility alias
  verticalAlign?: 'top'|'middle'|'bottom';   // default middle
  headerStyle?: Record<string,string|number>;
}

interface PivotDataOptions<Row extends object> {
  rows: Array<(keyof Row & string) | PivotField<Row>>;
  columns: Array<(keyof Row & string) | PivotField<Row>>;
  measures: PivotMeasure<Row>[];
  subtotals?: boolean;                      // default false
  grandTotals?: boolean | { rows?: boolean; columns?: boolean };
  emptyValue?: unknown;                     // default null
  subtotalLabel?: string | ((value, key, path) => string);
  grandTotalLabel?: string;                 // default 'Grand total'
}

interface PivotField<Row extends object> {
  key: keyof Row & string;
  header?: string;
  order?: 'asc'|'desc'|unknown[]|((a, b) => number);
  formatter?: (value: unknown) => string;
}

interface PivotMeasure<Row extends object> {
  key: keyof Row & string;
  header?: string;
  aggregate?: 'sum'|'average'|'avg'|'count'|'min'|'max' |
    ((values: unknown[], matchingRows: Row[]) => unknown);
  format?: string;
  sortable?: boolean | FacetTableColumnSortOptions<PivotTableRow>;
  filterable?: boolean | FacetTableColumnFilterOptions<PivotTableRow>;
  width?: number|string;
  horizontalAlign?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
  verticalAlign?: 'top'|'middle'|'bottom';
  style?: Record<string,string|number>;
  headerStyle?: Record<string,string|number>;
  chart?: FacetTableCellChartOptions<PivotTableRow>;
}

interface FacetTableCellChartOptions<Row extends object> {
  type?: ChartType;                         // default sparkline
  height?: number;                          // default 44px
  minWidth?: number;                        // default 120px
  scale?: 'independent'|'shared';           // default independent
  options?: Omit<ChartOptions,'series'>;
  series?: 'value' | ((value, row: Row, rowIndex: number) => SeriesOptions[]);
}

interface FacetTableCellDescriptor<Value = unknown> {
  value: Value;                             // raw value used by table behavior
  prefix?: string|number;                   // normal value cells only
  suffix?: string|number;                   // normal value cells only
  style?: Record<string,string|number>;     // arbitrary nested CSS
  [cssProperty: string]: unknown;           // direct color/background/etc.
}
```

### FacetTable multi-level column headers

Columns may be recursively grouped for pivot-style headers. A leaf column has
`key`; a group has `header` and `columns`. FacetTable calculates `colSpan` and
`rowSpan` automatically and flattens only leaf columns for body cells, sorting,
filtering, formatting, charts, widths, and borders.

```ts
new FacetTable('#pivot', {
  rows,
  columns: [
    { key: 'category', header: 'Category' },
    { key: 'product', header: 'Product' },
    { header: 'Bengaluru', columns: [
      { key: 'bengaluruRevenue', header: 'Revenue',
        format: '{value:,.2f}', sortable: true },
      { key: 'bengaluruAverage', header: 'Average Price',
        format: '{value:,.2f}', sortable: true },
    ] },
    { header: 'Chennai', columns: [
      { key: 'chennaiRevenue', header: 'Revenue',
        format: '{value:,.2f}', sortable: true },
      { key: 'chennaiAverage', header: 'Average Price',
        format: '{value:,.2f}', sortable: true },
    ] },
  ],
  style: {
    columnGroupHeader: { textAlign: 'center', fontWeight: 800 },
  },
});
```

Groups support arbitrary nesting, `horizontalAlign`, `verticalAlign`, and
`headerStyle`. `style.columnGroupHeader` styles all group headers. Sort and
filter controls belong only to leaf headings. Empty column groups are invalid.

### FacetTable pivotData transformer

`pivotData(rawRows, options)` converts raw records into FacetTable-ready
`{ rows, columns }`. Keep this transformation separate from the FacetTable
renderer:

```ts
import { FacetTable, pivotData } from 'facetviz';

const pivot = pivotData(salesRows, {
  rows: ['category', 'product'],
  columns: ['city'],
  measures: [
    { key: 'revenue', header: 'Revenue', aggregate: 'sum',
      format: '{value:$,.2f}', sortable: true },
    { key: 'unitPrice', header: 'Average Price', aggregate: 'average',
      format: '{value:,.2f}' },
  ],
  subtotals: true,
  grandTotals: true,
  emptyValue: null,
});

new FacetTable('#pivot', {
  ...pivot,
  pagination: { pageSize: 25 },
});
```

Built-in aggregates: `sum`, `average`/`avg`, `count`, `min`, `max`. Custom
aggregates receive `(values, matchingSourceRows)`. Totals always use matching
raw records, so averages/min/max/weighted values are not derived from displayed
subtotals.

Row and column field inputs may be keys or descriptors with `key`, `header`,
`formatter`, and `order`. `order` accepts `asc`, `desc`, an explicit value
array, or a comparator; omission retains first-source appearance. Multiple
column fields generate recursively nested header groups. Multiple measures
become leaf columns in every final group. Measures pass through format,
sorting, filtering, style, width, alignment, and chart options.

`grandTotals: true` adds both the total row and total column group. Use
`{rows:boolean, columns:boolean}` for independent control. `emptyValue` defaults
to null. Output rows include `rowType`/`groupPath`, and deterministic generated
keys avoid collisions with row fields and table metadata.

### FacetTable pre-grouped rows

FacetTable does not aggregate records. Supply detail, subtotal, and grand-total
rows already calculated by a database or application. Optional top-level row
metadata controls summary styling and group-safe sorting:

- `rowType: 'detail'|'subtotal'|'grandTotal'`
- `groupPath: unknown[]`

Rows with the same `groupPath` are sibling details. Sorting reorders only
those detail rows; subtotal and grand-total rows remain in their supplied
positions. Unmarked tables keep normal flat sorting.

```ts
new FacetTable('#sales', {
  rows: [
    { category: 'Beverages', product: 'Bread', city: 'Bengaluru',
      revenue: 949.19, rowType: 'detail',
      groupPath: ['Beverages', 'Bread'] },
    { category: 'Beverages', product: 'Bread', city: 'Chennai',
      revenue: 36797.68, rowType: 'detail',
      groupPath: ['Beverages', 'Bread'] },
    { category: 'Beverages', product: 'Bread — subtotal', city: '',
      revenue: 37746.87, rowType: 'subtotal',
      groupPath: ['Beverages', 'Bread'] },
    { category: 'Beverages — subtotal', product: '', city: '',
      revenue: 37746.87, rowType: 'subtotal',
      groupPath: ['Beverages'] },
    { category: 'Grand total', product: '', city: '',
      revenue: 59197.89, rowType: 'grandTotal', groupPath: [] },
  ],
  columns: [
    { key: 'category', header: 'Category' },
    { key: 'product', header: 'Product' },
    { key: 'city', header: 'City' },
    { key: 'revenue', header: 'SUM(Revenue)',
      format: '{value:,.2f}', sortable: true },
    { key: 'revenue', header: 'Revenue chart',
      chart: { type: 'bar', height: 28, scale: 'shared' } },
  ],
  style: {
    subtotalRow: { backgroundColor: '#f8fafc', fontWeight: 700 },
    grandTotalRow: { backgroundColor: '#f1f5f9', fontWeight: 800 },
  },
});
```

Never derive a grand total by adding displayed subtotals. Send the final
database/application result directly, especially for averages, minima, maxima,
and weighted calculations:

```ts
rows: [
  { category: 'Beverages', average: 15,
    rowType: 'subtotal', groupPath: ['Beverages'] },
  { category: 'Grocery', average: 100,
    rowType: 'subtotal', groupPath: ['Grocery'] },
  { category: 'Grand average', average: 43.33,
    rowType: 'grandTotal', groupPath: [] },
]
```

Summary rows expose `.facet-table-row-subtotal` and
`.facet-table-row-grand-total`, plus `data-row-type`. Use
`style.subtotalRow` and `style.grandTotalRow` for appearance. Filtering and
pagination operate on the rows exactly as supplied; recompute grouped results
outside FacetTable when a filter changes aggregate values.

`horizontalAlign` and `verticalAlign` apply to both the heading and body cells,
including chart cells. A sortable header's button follows the horizontal
alignment. A filterable header adds a funnel button and an accessible
Apply/Clear panel. `align` is an older alias; prefer `horizontalAlign` in new
code.

`format` uses the library's text-format syntax and receives `value`, `row`,
`rowIndex`, and `column`; dotted paths are supported. Examples:

```ts
{ key: 'revenue', format: '{value:$,.0f}' }
{ key: 'ratio', format: '{value:.1%}' }       // 0.124 -> 12.4%
{ key: 'score', format: '{row.product}: {value:,.1f}' }
```

Use `formatter` when formatting requires arbitrary logic or a DOM `Node`.
`formatter` takes precedence when both `formatter` and `format` are present.
Both are ignored for chart cells. Sorting and default filtering use raw cell
values, not the displayed formatted text. Default filtering is a
case-insensitive contains check. A filter object can supply a custom predicate;
multiple active column filters use AND logic and run before sorting and
pagination.

A row property may be a `FacetTableCellDescriptor`. Its `value` is unwrapped
before formatting, sorting, filtering, `style.cell` callbacks, or chart-series
construction. `prefix` and `suffix` wrap normal displayed values. All other
recognized CSS properties, plus the nested `style` map, apply only to that cell
and take precedence over table-wide styles. Example:

```ts
{ revenue: { value: 128400, color: 'red', backgroundColor: 'green',
             fontWeight: 900 },
  growth: { value: 12.4, prefix: '+', suffix: '%', color: '#45f354' } }
```

Column `style` applies to every body cell in that column and may be a CSS map or
`(value,row,rowIndex)=>CSSMap`; `headerStyle` applies to its heading. Body-cell
precedence from highest to lowest is: row cell descriptor, column `style`,
resolved top-level `style.row`, other top-level style slots, `layout`, then
`appearance`. Leaf heading precedence is `headerStyle`, `style.headerCell`,
layout, then appearance. Group heading precedence is group `headerStyle`,
`style.columnGroupHeader`, `style.headerCell`, layout, then appearance.

Structure and semantic appearance are separate from raw CSS overrides:

```ts
interface FacetTableLayoutOptions {
  tableLayout?: 'auto'|'fixed';
  rowDensity?: 'responsive'|'compact'|'cozy'|'crazy'|'comfortable';
  bodyTextSize?: number|string;
  showHeaderRow?: boolean;
  wrapText?: boolean;
  freezeHeaderRow?: boolean;
  freezeFirstColumn?: boolean;
}

interface FacetTableAppearanceOptions {
  headerRow?: {
    fillColor?: string; textColor?: string; textSize?: number|string;
    alignment?: 'left'|'center'|'right'; bold?: boolean; italic?: boolean;
  };
  rowsAndColumns?: {
    textColor?: string; rowFill?: string;
    dimensionAlignment?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
    valueAlignment?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
    displayEmptyCellAs?: string;
    bandedRows?: boolean; bandedRowsAlternateColor?: string;
    bandedColumns?: boolean; bandedColumnsAlternateColor?: string;
    emphasizeFirstColumn?: boolean; emphasizeLastColumn?: boolean;
    highlightRowOnHover?: boolean; hoverColor?: string;
  };
  borders?: {
    horizontalBorders?: boolean; verticalBorders?: boolean;
    outsideBorder?: boolean; borderColor?: string;
    borderWidth?: number|string;
  };
}
```

Responsive density uses compact padding below 600px, cozy padding from
600–899px, and comfortable padding at 900px or wider. `crazy` aliases `cozy`.
Numeric and chart cells infer role `value`; other cells infer `dimension`.
Explicit column alignment wins over role/header alignment. Low-level `style`
slots are applied after `layout` and `appearance` and may override their CSS.

### Cell charts and multi-series combo cells

When `chart.series` is omitted, an array cell value is one series' point data;
a scalar is wrapped as one point. The callback form can build any number of
series from the cell value or the entire row:

```ts
interface ComparisonRow {
  product: string;
  actual: number[];
  target: number[];
}

const columns: FacetTableColumn<ComparisonRow>[] = [
  { key: 'product', header: 'Product' },
  { key: 'actual', header: 'Actual + target', chart: {
    type: 'column', height: 100,
    series: (_value, row) => [
      { type: 'column', name: 'Actual', data: row.actual },
      { type: 'line', name: 'Target', data: row.target,
        marker: { enabled: true } },
    ],
    options: {
      xAxis: { categories: ['Q1','Q2','Q3','Q4'] },
      legend: { enabled: true },
      tooltip: { shared: true },
    },
  } },
];
```

For JSON-only configurations, store a complete `SeriesOptions[]` in the cell
and set `series:'value'`:

```ts
{
  rows: [{
    product: 'Atlas',
    comparison: [
      { type: 'column', name: 'Actual', data: [22,28,31,38] },
      { type: 'line', name: 'Target', data: [24,27,33,36] },
    ],
  }],
  columns: [
    { key: 'product' },
    { key: 'comparison', chart: { type: 'column', series: 'value' } },
  ],
}
```

Axes, legend, background, animation, responsive font scaling, and per-chart
resize observation are disabled/minimized by default for compact cell charts.
Override axes, legend, tooltip, and plot settings through `chart.options`.
Set `xAxis.visible:true`/`yAxis.visible:true` when axes should be drawn.
FacetTable uses one ResizeObserver for the whole table. `scale:'shared'` computes
one value-axis domain from all rows in that chart column, including rows on
other pages; use it when magnitudes must be comparable. `independent` emphasizes
each row's shape. Only charts on the visible page are mounted. Unless explicitly
provided, each cell chart receives an accessibility description derived from
the chart-column heading and the first non-chart value in its row.

### Sorting, pagination, and table styling

Sortable headers cycle ascending -> descending -> original row order. Sorting
is stable, happens before pagination, resets to page 1, uses natural comparison
for numbers/dates/booleans/text, and keeps nullish values last. Supply `compare`
for domain-specific or formatted-string values.

```ts
pagination: true // 25 rows/page; choices 10,25,50,100

pagination: {
  enabled: true,
  pageSize: 25,
  page: 1,
  pageSizeOptions: [10,25,50,100],
  showPageSize: true,
  showPageNumbers: true,
  maxPageButtons: 5,
  alwaysShow: false,
  align: 'right',
  labels: { first: 'First', previous: 'Previous', next: 'Next', last: 'Last',
            page: 'Page', of: 'of', rows: 'rows', perPage: 'Rows per page' },
  onPageChange: (page, pageSize) => {},
}
```

For any table that may grow into thousands of rows, generate a pagination
configuration instead of mounting every row. FacetTable caches filtered and
sorted row sets, but it intentionally renders native semantic table elements
and does not virtualize the DOM. Only cell charts on the visible page mount.

Row pagination does not reduce pivot width. Estimate pivot value columns as
the product of distinct column-field combinations times the number of measures.
For example, 20 cities x four quarters x two measures creates 160 value
columns. Filter or pre-aggregate high-cardinality column fields before calling
`pivotData()` when that result would be too wide to read.

`style` accepts CSS property maps. Numeric dimensional values become pixels;
recognized unitless properties and CSS custom properties remain as supplied.
Available slots:

```txt
root, table, caption, head, headerRow, headerCell, columnGroupHeader, headerControls, sortButton,
sortIndicator, filterButton, activeFilterButton, filterIndicator, filterPanel,
filterInput, filterActions, filterActionButton, body, row, cell, valueCell,
chartCell, chartHost, emptyCell, pagination,
paginationInfo, paginationButton, activePageButton, pageSizeLabel, pageSizeSelect
```

`row` may be a style map or `(row,rowIndex)=>style`. `cell` may be a style map
or `(value,row,rowIndex,column)=>style`; use these for stripes and conditional
formatting without changing source data.

### FacetTable runtime API

```ts
table.setRows(nextRows);
table.update({ columns, style, pagination });
table.page;                                // current 1-based page
table.pageSize;
table.pageCount;
table.setPage(2);
table.setPageSize(50);
table.sort;                                // {key,direction} | undefined
table.sortBy('revenue', 'desc');           // column must be sortable
table.clearSort();
table.filters;                             // [{key,value}, ...]
table.setFilter('product', 'atlas');       // column must be filterable
table.clearFilter('product');
table.clearFilters();
table.charts;                              // FacetViz[] mounted on current page
table.reflow();
table.destroy();
```

FacetTable renders native `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `th`, and `td` elements;
do not replace it with a grid of unrelated SVG charts when table semantics,
selection, or screen-reader navigation matter. Keep cell charts compact, avoid
repeating titles in every cell, and enable legends only when multiple series
cannot be understood from surrounding headings/context.

## Choose the chart type

Use this decision order:

| Analytical goal | Recommended type | Use when | Avoid when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compare categories | `column` | Few ordered categories, vertical labels fit | Many/long labels |
| Compare categories with long labels | `bar` | Labels read better horizontally | Time trends |
| Rank one measure | `lollipop` or `bar` | A lighter alternative to bars | Stacked totals |
| Trend over ordered/time x | `line` | Exact progression matters | Unordered categories |
| Smooth visual trend | `spline` | Presentation-focused trend | Overshoot could mislead |
| Discrete state changes | `step` | Values remain constant between changes | Smooth measurements |
| Magnitude over time | `area` | One/few series and baseline matters | Many overlapping series |
| Part-to-whole over categories | stacked `column`/`bar` | Compare totals and components | Only one total |
| Percentage composition | `stacking:'percent'` or `marimekko` | Relative shares matter | Absolute values matter more |
| One small part-to-whole | `pie`/`donut` | 2–6 positive slices | Many slices or close comparisons |
| Relationship between two numbers | `scatter` | x and y are continuous | Categorical x |
| Relationship plus magnitude | `bubble` | z is meaningful and nonnegative | Precise z comparisons |
| Distribution of raw values | `histogram` | Raw numeric observations | Already aggregated bins |
| Distribution by category | `boxplot` | Five-number summaries/outliers | Audience cannot read boxplots |
| Show overlapping category values | `jitter` | Individual observations matter | Very large datasets |
| Compare low/high endpoints | `dumbbell` | Before/after or two measures | Long time series |
| Compare two time/category endpoints | `slope` | Few series, usually two x categories | Many crossings/series |
| Uncertainty/range | `arearange`, `columnrange`, `errorbar` | Low/high bounds are primary | Only a single value exists |
| Financial OHLC | `candlestick` | open/high/low/close data | Generic ranges |
| Running contributions | `waterfall` | Deltas build toward totals | Independent categories |
| Progress against targets | `bullet` | Measure, target, qualitative ranges | Multiple time points |
| One or a few KPIs on dials | `gauge` | Bounded values share one range | Many precise comparisons |
| Events on a sequence | `timeline` | Event order/timing is primary | Durations matter |
| Tasks with durations | `gantt` | start/end per task | Dependencies/critical path required |
| Category × category intensity | `heatmap` | Dense matrix comparison | Precise individual values |
| Daily activity | `calendar` | Date/value contribution-style grid | Irregular non-daily data |
| Stages narrowing | `funnel` | Ordered conversion stages | Non-sequential categories |
| Hierarchical structure | `treegraph` | Parent-child topology matters | Part-to-whole area matters |
| Hierarchical proportions | `sunburst` | Nested share and hierarchy matter | Precise cross-branch comparison |
| Weighted flows | `sankey` | Acyclic source→target flow | Cyclic graphs |
| Multivariate radial profile | `radar` | Few series and 3–8 comparable metrics | Different units/scales |
| Back-to-back comparison | `butterfly` | Two populations share categories | More than two main series |
| Tiny inline trend | `sparkline` | Table/card context already labels it | Standalone analytical chart |
| Repeated comparable panels | `trellis` | Same measure across dimensions | Non-cartesian cross-tab panels |

Default to `line` for a genuine ordered trend and `column`/`bar` for categorical
comparison. Never choose pie/donut solely because values sum to 100; use it only
when the user needs a simple part-to-whole view.

Supported `ChartType` values (exact spelling):

```txt
line, spline, step, area, areaspline, arearange, areasplinerange,
column, bar, columnrange, waterfall, histogram, bullet, lollipop,
scatter, jitter, bubble, boxplot, dumbbell, slope, candlestick, errorbar,
pie, donut, radialbar, gauge, radar, funnel, sunburst,
heatmap, calendar, timeline, gantt, treegraph, sankey,
butterfly, marimekko, sparkline
```

`radar`, `butterfly`, `marimekko`, and `sparkline` depend on chart-level layout
behavior; set them as `chart.type`, not only as an isolated `series.type`.

## Root options

```ts
interface ChartOptions {
  chart?: {
    type?: ChartType;                         // default 'line'
    width?: number; height?: number;          // defaults to container size, then 640×400
    backgroundColor?: string;
    spacing?: [number, number, number, number]; // top right bottom left
    inverted?: boolean;
    polar?: boolean;                          // line/area/scatter/column/dumbbell families
    polarInnerSize?: number|string;           // pixels or e.g. '35%'
    polarInnerBackgroundColor?: string;       // e.g. '#fff'
    polarGridLineMode?: 'spoke'|'sector';     // category centres or boundaries
    colors?: string[];
    animation?: boolean | { enabled?: boolean; duration?: number; easing?: string };
    zoom?: 'x' | 'y' | 'xy' | false | { type?: 'x'|'y'|'xy'|false };
    reflow?: boolean;                         // default true
    responsive?: boolean;                     // default true; hides data labels when short side <180px
    scaleFonts?: boolean;                     // default true; false keeps explicit fontSize values literal
    boost?: boolean | { enabled?: boolean; threshold?: number };
    events?: { render?; click? };
  };
  title?: { text?: string; enabled?: boolean; align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
            margin?: number; offsetY?: number; style?: Record<string,string> };
  subtitle?: { text?: string; enabled?: boolean; align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
               margin?: number; offsetY?: number; style?: Record<string,string> };
  xAxis?: AxisOptions | AxisOptions[];
  yAxis?: AxisOptions | AxisOptions[];
  tooltip?: TooltipOptions;
  legend?: LegendOptions;
  plotOptions?: { series?: Partial<SeriesOptions>; [type: string]: Partial<SeriesOptions>|undefined };
  series: SeriesOptions[];                    // REQUIRED
  colors?: string[];                          // palette; chart.colors has precedence
  theme?: 'light'|'dark'|'high-contrast'|'pastel'|ThemeObject;
  trellis?: { columns?: string; rows?: string; gap?: number;
              sharedX?: boolean; sharedY?: boolean; table?: boolean };
  annotations?: Array<{ x?: number|string; y?: number; text?: string;
    shape?: 'label'|'callout'|'circle'; dx?: number; dy?: number;
    xAxis?: 0|1; yAxis?: 0|1; zIndex?: 'above'|'below' }>;
  texts?: Array<{ text: string; enabled?: boolean; align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
    verticalAlign?: 'top'|'center'|'bottom';
    offsetX?: number; offsetY?: number; color?: string; style?: Record<string,string>;
    lineHeight?: number; rotation?: number; className?: string }>;
  responsive?: Array<{
    condition: { minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: number;
                 minHeight?: number; maxHeight?: number };
    options: Partial<ChartOptions>;            // layout options; no series replacement
  }>;
  drilldown?: { series: Array<SeriesOptions & { id: string }> };
  accessibility?: {
    enabled?: boolean;
    description?: string;
    keyboardNavigation?: boolean;             // default true
    pointDescriptionFormatter?: (ctx: {
      seriesName: string; seriesIndex: number; pointIndex: number;
      x: number|string; y?: number; low?: number; high?: number; point: PointOptions;
    }) => string;
  };
  validation?: boolean | {
    mode?: 'warn'|'error'|'silent';
    onIssue?: (issue: { code: string; severity: 'error'|'warning';
                        path: string; message: string; suggestion?: string }) => void;
  };
  seriesEvents?: { click?; mouseOver?; mouseOut?; legendItemClick? };
}
```

### Axis options

```ts
interface AxisOptions {
  visible?: boolean;
  opposite?: boolean;                        // x→top, y→right
  categories?: string[];
  type?: 'linear'|'log'|'category'|'datetime';
  title?: { text?: string; enabled?: boolean;
    align?: 'start'|'center'|'end'; margin?: number; offset?: number;
    position?: 'outer'|'center';             // polar x-axis only
    style?: Record<string,string> };
  min?: number; max?: number; tickCount?: number;
  labels?: {
    enabled?: boolean;
    format?: string;
    formatter?: (value: number|string) => string;
    rotation?: number;
    autoRotation?: number[];
    step?: number;
    maxWidth?: number;
    overflow?: 'ellipsis'|'hide';
    position?: 'outer'|'inner';              // non-inverted polar x-axis
    offset?: number;                         // polar label gap in pixels
    style?: Record<string,string>;
  };
  crosshair?: boolean;
  gridLineWidth?: number; gridLineColor?: string; gridLineDashStyle?: string;
  alternateGridColor?: string;               // every other category band
  minorTickInterval?: number|'auto';
  minorGridLineWidth?: number; minorGridLineColor?: string;
  minorGridLineDashStyle?: string;
  lineWidth?: number; lineColor?: string; ticks?: boolean;
  reversed?: boolean;
  plotLines?: Array<{ value: number|string; color?: string; width?: number;
    dashStyle?: string; zIndex?: 'above'|'below';
    label?: { text: string; align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
      verticalAlign?: 'above'|'below'; color?: string } }>;
  plotBands?: Array<{ from: number|string; to: number|string; color?: string;
    label?: { text: string; color?: string } }>;
  dimension?: string;
  dimensions?: string[];
  aggregate?: 'sum'|'avg'|'count'|'min'|'max';
}
```

### Series options

```ts
interface SeriesOptions {
  type?: ChartType;
  name?: string;
  data: PointInput[];
  color?: string;
  fillColor?: string | {
    linearGradient: { x1?: number|string; y1?: number|string;
      x2?: number|string; y2?: number|string;
      gradientUnits?: 'objectBoundingBox'|'userSpaceOnUse' };
    stops: Array<[number|string, string] | [number|string, string, number]>;
  }; // area / areaspline
  visible?: boolean; showInLegend?: boolean;
  stack?: string|number; stacking?: 'normal'|'percent';
  startAngle?: number; endAngle?: number;        // radialbar or gauge degrees
  xAxis?: 0 | 1; yAxis?: 0 | 1;
  lineWidth?: number; size?: number;
  marker?: { enabled?: boolean; radius?: number;
    symbol?: 'circle'|'square'|'diamond'|'triangle'|'rectangle';
    fillColor?: string; lineColor?: string; lineWidth?: number;
    width?: number; height?: number };
  dataLabels?: { enabled?: boolean; format?: string; formatter?: (ctx)=>string;
    color?: string; fontSize?: string; fontWeight?: string;
    align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
    position?: 'outside'|'inside'|'center'|'base'|'top'|'bottom'|'left'|'right';
    distance?: number; rotation?: number; backgroundColor?: string };
  tooltip?: { enabled?: boolean; format?: string; formatter?: (ctx)=>string;
    valuePrefix?: string; valueSuffix?: string; valueDecimals?: number };
  states?: { hover?: { enabled?: boolean; scale?: number; brightness?: number } };
  // gauge series
  min?: number; max?: number;
  minLabel?: string; maxLabel?: string;
  trackColor?: string; trackOpacity?: number; thickness?: number; roundedEnds?: boolean;
  showMinMax?: boolean; showMinLabel?: boolean; showMaxLabel?: boolean;
  centerFormatter?: (value: number) => string;
  centerFontSize?: number;
  namePosition?: 'top'|'center'|'bottom'; // top/bottom centres the value
  markers?: Array<{
    value: number; label?: string; color?: string;
    labelPosition?: 'outside'|'inside'; fontSize?: number;
  }>;
}
```

```ts
interface TooltipOptions {
  enabled?: boolean;
  shared?: boolean;
  format?: string;
  formatter?: (ctx) => string;
  backgroundColor?: string; borderColor?: string; color?: string;
  valuePrefix?: string; valueSuffix?: string; valueDecimals?: number;
}

interface LegendOptions {
  enabled?: boolean;
  align?: 'left'|'center'|'right';
  verticalAlign?: 'top'|'bottom';
  layout?: 'horizontal'|'vertical';
  itemStyle?: Record<string,string>;
}

interface ThemeObject {
  base?: 'light'|'dark'|'high-contrast'|'pastel'|string;
  colors?: string[];
  backgroundColor?: string;
  fontFamily?: string;
  title?: { color?: string; fontSize?: string; fontWeight?: string };
  subtitle?: { color?: string; fontSize?: string };
  axis?: { labelColor?: string; titleColor?: string;
    lineColor?: string; gridLineColor?: string };
  dataLabel?: { color?: string };
  legend?: { color?: string; hiddenColor?: string };
  tooltip?: { backgroundColor?: string; borderColor?: string; color?: string };
  neutralColor?: string;
}
```

`plotOptions.series` applies to every series; `plotOptions[type]` applies to
that type; explicit series options win. Use `plotOptions` instead of repeating
identical label, marker, stacking, or tooltip settings.

## Point data shapes

```ts
type PointInput =
  | number                       // y; x comes from category or index
  | [number|string, number]      // [x,y]
  | [number|string, number, number] // [x,low,high]
  | { x?, y?, name?, color?, ...typeSpecificFields }
  | null;                        // line/area gap
```

Rules:

- For categorical series, prefer `xAxis.categories` plus aligned numeric arrays
  when every series has every category.
- Use object or tuple points when categories are missing/reordered. Stacking is
  matched by actual x value.
- For numeric/time x, use `[x,y]` or `{x,y}` and do not stringify x.
- Datetime x values are millisecond timestamps. Use `Date.UTC(...)` when time
  zones should not alter the date.
- Use `null` to create a visible break in line/area data.
- Avoid `NaN`, `Infinity`, mixed units, and duplicate x values unless intentional.

## Exact data for each specialized type

```ts
// column, bar, line, spline, step, area, lollipop, slope, radar, sparkline
data: [5, 3, 8]                         // pair with xAxis.categories
data: [['Jan', 5], ['Feb', 3]]

// range, columnrange, errorbar, dumbbell
data: [['A', 10, 18], ['B', 7, 15]]    // [x,low,high]

// pie, donut, radialbar, funnel
data: [{ name: 'A', y: 42 }, { name: 'B', y: 58 }]

// scatter / jitter / bubble
data: [{ x: 2, y: 8 }]                  // scatter
data: [{ x: 'Group A', y: 8 }]          // jitter
data: [{ x: 2, y: 8, z: 30 }]           // bubble

// boxplot
data: [{ x: 'A', min: 2, q1: 4, median: 6, q3: 8, max: 11,
         outliers: [15] }]

// candlestick
data: [{ x: timestamp, open: 100, high: 112, low: 96, close: 108 }]

// waterfall
data: [{ x: 'Revenue', y: 120 }, { x: 'Costs', y: -45 },
       { x: 'Profit', y: 0, isSum: true }]

// histogram (bins must be a positive integer when provided)
{ type: 'histogram', bins: 12, data: [12.1, 13.7, 11.8, ...] }

// marimekko: one aligned value per category in each series; column width is
// derived from that category's total and each column is 100% stacked
xAxis: { categories: ['A','B','C'] }
series: [{ name: 'Online', data: [30,50,20] },
         { name: 'Retail', data: [20,10,40] }]

// butterfly: exactly two main series mirrored around a shared category axis
xAxis: { categories: ['18–24','25–34','35–44'] }
series: [{ name: 'Group A', data: [18,25,20] },
         { name: 'Group B', data: [16,28,23] }]

// bullet
data: [{ name: 'Revenue', y: 72, target: 80, ranges: [50, 75, 100] }]

// gauge: values lay out left-to-right; chart.inverted makes them top-to-bottom
// marker fontSize is a pixel value; point color overrides the series color
plotOptions: { gauge: {
  color: '#22c55e',
  markers: [{ value: 80, label: 'Target', fontSize: 12 }]
} }
series: [{ type: 'gauge', min: 0, max: 100,
  data: [{ name: 'API', y: 86 }, { name: 'Workers', y: 74 }] }]

// Full-circle gauge; hide just the minimum label when desired
series: [{ type: 'gauge', min: 0, max: 100,
  startAngle: -90, endAngle: 270, showMinLabel: false, roundedEnds: true,
  namePosition: 'bottom',
  data: [{ name: 'API', y: 86 }] }]

// heatmap
data: [{ x: 'Mon', y: 'Morning', value: 18 }]

// calendar
data: [{ date: new Date(2026, 6, 21).getTime(), value: 8 }]

// timeline (events are evenly spaced and x is displayed as its label)
data: [{ x: '2026-01-01', name: 'Launch', description: 'v1' }]

// gantt
data: [{ name: 'Design', start: Date.UTC(2026,0,1), end: Date.UTC(2026,0,12) }]

// treegraph / sunburst
data: [{ id: 'root', name: 'Company' },
       { id: 'sales', parent: 'root', name: 'Sales', value: 30 }]

// sankey: positive weights and an acyclic graph are required
data: [{ from: 'Visit', to: 'Trial', weight: 240 },
       { from: 'Trial', to: 'Paid', weight: 80 }]
```

Type-specific series options:

- `pie`/`donut`: `innerSize:'60%'`; optional `dimensions:['parent','child']`;
  point `z` creates variable-radius slices.
- `bubble`: `sizeRange:[6,34]`.
- `jitter`: `jitter:0.5` is spread in category-band units.
- `boxplot`: `boxColors:{lower,upper,median,whisker,border}` and
  `outlierMarker`.
- `dumbbell`: `lowColor`, `highColor`, `connectorColor`, `connectorWidth`.
- `radar`/`area`: `fillOpacity` where applicable.
- `sparkline`: `sparkline:{last?,min?,max?}`.

## Option-selection heuristics

### Titles and axes

- Title the question or measure, not the chart type: “Monthly revenue”, not
  “Column chart”.
- Put units in axis titles: `Revenue (USD)`, `Latency (ms)`, `Conversion (%)`.
- Use `xAxis.type:'datetime'` for time values and `crosshair:true` for dense
  trends.
- Rotate category labels only when necessary: `-45` first, `-90` as a last
  resort. Prefer `bar` for many long labels.
- Do not set `min`/`max` unless the analytical range is intentional. Explicit
  bounds are exact and can clip data.
- Use a log axis only for strictly positive values spanning orders of magnitude.
- Use `plotLines` for targets/benchmarks and `plotBands` for meaningful ranges;
  use `zIndex:'above'` when marks could cover a reference line.

### Color and theme

- Prefer `theme` or a root palette over repeated series colors.
- Built-ins: `'light'`, `'dark'`, `'high-contrast'`, `'pastel'`.
- `chart.colors` overrides top-level `colors`, which overrides theme colors.
- An explicit `series.color` intentionally opts that series out of later palette
  changes.
- Use consistent color for the same concept across charts. Do not rely on color
  alone for meaning; names, labels, or position must carry the distinction.
- Use `high-contrast` and an accessibility description when accessibility is a
  priority.
- SVG points are keyboard navigable by default: Tab enters once; Arrow keys move
  between points; Home/End jump; Enter/Space activate. Preserve this behavior
  unless the surrounding application supplies an equivalent interaction model.
- Use `accessibility.pointDescriptionFormatter` when domain context or units are
  not clear from the generated series/category/value label.

### Labels, legend, and tooltip

- Enable data labels for sparse summary charts, not dense line/scatter charts.
- Prefer `dataLabels.position:'inside'` only when marks are large enough.
- Stacked bars default labels to the segment center; this is usually correct.
- Use `tooltip.shared:true` for aligned multi-series x values with the same
  unit. For dual-axis series with different units, prefer individual tooltips.
- Use `legend.enabled:false` for a single obvious series. Single-series
  point-legend charts (`pie`, `donut`, `radialbar`) still benefit from a legend
  when labels are not shown; stacked radial bars use one legend item per series.
- Default tooltip formatting safely escapes substituted data. A custom
  `tooltip.formatter` returns trusted HTML; never insert untrusted strings into
  it without escaping.

Formatting tokens for labels/tooltips: `{x}`, `{y}`, `{name}`, `{series}`,
`{percentage}`, `{total}`, `{low}`, `{high}`, `{point.<field>}`. Axis labels use
`{value}`. Examples: `{y:$,.1f}`, `{y:.0%}`, `{y:,.1s}`, `{x:%b %d}`.

### Performance and responsiveness

- Leave `chart.reflow:true` for normal responsive layouts.
- With `chart.responsive` enabled (the default), data labels are hidden when
  the chart's shorter side is below 180px and return automatically when it grows.
  Set `chart.responsive:false` to keep configured labels at every size.
- Use root `responsive` rules for size-specific legend, title, axis, tooltip,
  trellis, annotation, chart text, or accessibility overrides. Rules match the rendered
  width/height and do not mutate the stored options.
- Call `chart.reflow()` after a hidden tab, grid, or resizable panel becomes
  visible or finishes layout.
- Boost auto-enables beyond 1500 points for supported cartesian line/point
  series. Do not force it for small charts.
- Boosted canvas pixels are embedded into SVG/PNG exports.
- Disable animation in tests, server-generated screenshots, or rapid update
  loops: `chart:{animation:false}`.

### General polar projection

Set `chart.polar:true` to project `line`, `spline`, `step`, `area`,
`areaspline`, `scatter`, `jitter`, `column`, or `dumbbell` series into a shared
angular x-axis / radial y-axis. Polar dumbbells connect each low/high pair
radially at its category angle. Tooltips, events, stacking, labels, annotations,
legends, and a second y scale continue to work. Use dedicated `radar`,
`radialbar`, and `gauge` types for their specialized semantics.
`radialbar` supports `stacking:'normal'|'percent'`. Matching point names/x
values share a ring, and every series arc continues from the previous one:

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'radialbar' },
  series: [
    { name: 'Done', stacking: 'normal', data: [{ name: 'Move', y: 60 }, { name: 'Exercise', y: 35 }] },
    { name: 'Remaining', stacking: 'normal', data: [{ name: 'Move', y: 20 }, { name: 'Exercise', y: 25 }] }
  ]
}
```
Radial-bar angles are configurable in degrees. Use
`plotOptions:{radialbar:{startAngle:-90,endAngle:90}}` for a half circle. The
default is `-90` through `180` (a 270° sweep); sweeps up to 360° are supported.
Add `chart.inverted:true` to swap the roles: x is radial/vertical and y is
circular/angular. In this mode columns are concentric arcs and dumbbell
connectors follow circular arcs.
Add `chart.polarInnerSize:'35%'` for a donut-style centre hole and
`polarInnerBackgroundColor:'#fff'` for an explicitly white circle.
Use `polarGridLineMode:'sector'` to outline category wedges with boundary
dividers instead of drawing spokes through category centres.
For a donut-style polar layout, use `xAxis.labels.position:'inner'` to curve
category labels around the centre-hole radius. Add `xAxis.labels.offset` for
the pixel gap from that circle, and use
`xAxis.title.position:'center'` to put the x-axis title in the middle.

## Composition patterns

### Grouped and stacked columns

Series without `stacking` group side-by-side. Apply stacking to every series in
the same stack.

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'column' },
  title: { text: 'Quarterly revenue by region' },
  xAxis: { categories: ['Q1','Q2','Q3','Q4'], title: { text: 'Quarter' } },
  yAxis: { title: { text: 'Revenue (USD)' } },
  tooltip: { shared: true, valuePrefix: '$', valueDecimals: 0 },
  plotOptions: { column: { stacking: 'normal' } },
  series: [
    { name: 'North', stack: 'revenue', data: [12,15,14,18] },
    { name: 'South', stack: 'revenue', data: [9,11,13,14] },
  ],
  accessibility: { description: 'Quarterly revenue split between North and South regions.' },
}
```

### Datetime trend with zoom

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'line', zoom: 'x' },
  title: { text: 'Daily response time' },
  xAxis: { type: 'datetime', crosshair: true, title: { text: 'Date' } },
  yAxis: { title: { text: 'Response time (ms)' } },
  tooltip: { shared: true, valueSuffix: ' ms', valueDecimals: 1 },
  series: [{ name: 'p95', data: [[Date.UTC(2026,6,1),128], ...] }],
}
```

### Combo chart with a secondary axis

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'column' },
  xAxis: { categories: months },
  yAxis: [
    { title: { text: 'Orders' } },
    { title: { text: 'Conversion (%)' }, opposite: true },
  ],
  series: [
    { name: 'Orders', data: orderCounts },
    { type: 'spline', name: 'Conversion', yAxis: 1, data: conversionRates,
      tooltip: { valueSuffix: '%' } },
  ],
}
```

### Nested categories

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'column' },
  xAxis: { dimensions: ['Region','Category'], aggregate: 'sum' },
  yAxis: { title: { text: 'Sales' } },
  series: [{ name: 'Sales', data: [
    { Region: 'East', Category: 'Tech', y: 12 },
    { Region: 'East', Category: 'Office', y: 8 },
  ] }],
}
```

### Small multiples

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'line' },
  trellis: { columns: 'product', rows: 'region', sharedX: true, sharedY: true },
  series: [{ name: 'Sales', data: [
    { x: 'Jan', y: 12, product: 'A', region: 'East' },
    { x: 'Feb', y: 15, product: 'A', region: 'East' },
  ] }],
}
```

Cross-tab trellis (`table` default `true`) is for cartesian types. For pie,
donut, sunburst, gauge, and other non-cartesian types, use
`trellis:{columns:'field',table:false}` or separate chart instances.

### Drilldown

```ts
{
  chart: { type: 'column' },
  series: [{ name: 'Products', data: [
    { name: 'Hardware', y: 40, drilldown: 'hardware' },
  ] }],
  drilldown: { series: [
    { id: 'hardware', name: 'Hardware', data: [['Laptops',25],['Desktops',15]] },
  ] },
}
```

## Live API

```ts
chart.update(partialOptions);            // deep-merge, re-resolve, render
chart.setData(seriesIndex, data);         // preserve runtime visibility
chart.addPoint(seriesIndex, point);
chart.appendData(seriesIndex, points, { maxPoints: 2_000 });
chart.batchUpdate((batch) => {            // synchronous; one final render
  batch.appendData(0, pointsA, { maxPoints: 2_000 });
  batch.appendData(1, pointsB, { maxPoints: 2_000 });
});
chart.setSize(width, height);
chart.reflow();
chart.drillUp();
chart.on('point:click', listener);         // returns unsubscribe function
chart.getSVG();
chart.downloadSVG(filename?);
chart.downloadPNG(filename?, scale?);
chart.toPNGBlob(scale?);
chart.legendItems;
chart.hasLegend;
chart.destroy();
```

For live or streaming charts, prefer `appendData()` over repeatedly copying the
entire data array into `setData()`. Set `maxPoints` to an explicit positive
integer so long-lived dashboards have bounded memory; it limits raw source rows
before rendering. Wrap related series/options changes in `batchUpdate()` so
validation, rebuilding, and rendering occur once. The callback
must be synchronous. Batches can nest, and thrown callbacks roll back their
level. Streaming preserves series visibility and active single-axis zoom.

For palette/theme changes, use `chart.update({theme})` or
`chart.update({colors:[...]})`; existing cartesian and point-based series are
recolored. Keep a reference to the chart and call `destroy()` when its UI owner
unmounts.

## Validation checklist

Before returning generated chart code, verify:

- A FacetTable has non-empty `columns`, every column key belongs to the row
  schema (with missing values intentional), pagination values are positive
  integers, and `series:'value'` cells contain `SeriesOptions[]` rather than
  ordinary point arrays.
- FacetTable formatting and sorting use raw typed values (especially numbers and
  dates); do not pre-format source values merely to control their display.
- `series` exists, every series has `data`, and every `type` is supported.
- `xAxis.categories.length` matches aligned numeric arrays.
- Every range has `low <= high`; every boxplot has
  `min <= q1 <= median <= q3 <= max`.
- Pie/funnel/radial values and Sankey weights are positive where required.
- Histogram `bins` is a positive integer.
- Sankey and hierarchy IDs are valid; Sankey links are acyclic.
- Datetime x/start/end values are milliseconds and Gantt `end > start`.
- Secondary-axis series use `yAxis:1` and top-level `yAxis` has two entries.
- Stacked series share the intended x values and stacking mode.
- Percent data is not accidentally multiplied twice (`.0%` multiplies by 100;
  use it for ratios such as `0.42`, not values already equal to `42`).
- Log axes contain no zero or negative values.
- Data labels will not overwhelm the marks.
- Long category labels use `bar`, rotation, thinning, or fewer categories.
- Colors have adequate contrast against `chart.backgroundColor`.
- The accessibility description explains the key measure and grouping.
- Custom point descriptions include domain meaning and units when the defaults
  are insufficient.
- `validateChartOptions()` returns no errors. Treat its stable `path` as the
  field to repair and its `code` as the machine-readable failure category;
  warnings should be reviewed but do not make the configuration invalid.
- Application code updates or destroys an existing chart rather than stacking
  multiple SVG roots in one container.
- Library changes that touch rendering, layout, point normalization, or boost
  preserve the automated budgets: 1,200 SVG points, 100k boosted points, and a
  100k live update must each complete under one second in the browser suite;
  boosted cases must remain below 200 DOM nodes. The bundled library must stay
  below 280 kB raw and 70 kB gzip.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Do not manually mount one independent FacetViz instance per HTML table cell;
  use FacetTable so chart cleanup, reflow, pagination, shared scales, and table
  semantics remain coordinated.
- Do not repeat axes, titles, and legends in every tiny cell chart unless the
  cell dimensions and missing surrounding context genuinely require them.
- Do not use `chart.type:'bar'` together with manual negative values merely to
  make bars point left; `bar` already means horizontal orientation.
- Do not use categorical string x values for a continuous scatter/time axis.
- Do not set `yAxis.min:0` on boxplot, dumbbell, candlestick, or range charts
  unless zero is analytically meaningful; these types auto-pad their extent.
- Do not add a zero baseline manually for `column`, `bar`, `area`, `areaspline`,
  `errorbar`, or `lollipop`; they already include it.
- Do not use `trellis.table:true` for non-cartesian charts.
- Do not enable markers and data labels for thousands of line points.
- Do not hard-code a series color if it should respond to palette/theme updates.
- Do not rely on legend color alone to explain a chart.
- Do not pass raw HTML from untrusted data through a tooltip formatter.
- Do not guess unsupported options from another charting library; consult
  `docs/API.md` when an option is not listed here.
